question.text: An investor invested Rs. 2,00,000 in an equity fund when the NAV was Rs. 100. After 2 years, the NAV has grown to Rs. 130. During this period, the scheme's TER was 2% per annum. What was the approximate gross return (before TER) per annum that the scheme's portfolio generated?

explanation.text: The Logic: Returns over periods greater than one year are computed on a compounded (CAGR) basis per the NISM Series V-A workbook (pp.39, 249, 252). NAV grew from Rs. 100 to Rs. 130 over 2 years. Net CAGR = (130/100)^(1/2) - 1 = sqrt(1.30) - 1 = approximately 14.02% per annum. Since NAV is net of TER (p.39), gross return per annum = net CAGR + TER = 14.02% + 2% = approximately 16.02% per annum. The Trap: 15% is the simple-average annualization that ignores compounding. 13% wrongly subtracts TER from the net return instead of adding it back. 30% is the cumulative 2-year return without annualizing. Note: When evaluating fund-manager performance, look at gross return (before TER) to assess stock-picking skill, but quote net returns to clients since that is what they earn. A fund with high gross returns but very high TER may deliver lower net returns than a peer with moderate gross returns and a low TER.
